name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male official responsible for half the district of Keilah, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:17. Beyond his administrative role, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribal affiliation or personal background. His mention highlights his part in the organized efforts during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's sovereignty. This proper name, as given in Nehemiah 3:17, does not indicate that it was divinely assigned but reveals a common practice of embedding God's name within personal names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hashabiah beyond his role as an official in Keilah. There are no listed relatives or connections in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his role as an official overseeing half of Keilah during the reconstruction efforts described in Nehemiah. His leadership position underscores the organized nature of the community's restoration work under God's providence. Although not a major biblical figure, his mention contributes to the historical and spiritual context of Israel's return and rebuilding.
